name: Primary Immunodeficiency
remarks: Models the lifetime course of primary immunodeficiency disorder (PID) with branching for severity, infections, and treatment.
Code provenance (all verified April 2026):
- SNOMED 58606001 (Primary immune deficiency disorder) — verified via snomedbrowser.com (Read Code X20Ga; ICD-10 D80-D84)
- SNOMED 234336002 (Hemopoietic stem cell transplant) — verified via OpenSAFELY BMT codelist + NIH VSAC
- SNOMED 50849002 (Emergency room admission) — official Synthea wiki canonical example
- SNOMED 32485007 (Hospital admission) — verified via NCBO BioPortal
- SNOMED 185349003 (Encounter for symptom) — used in Synthea base modules
- SNOMED 11429006 (Consultation) — used in Synthea base modules
- SNOMED 12295008 (Bronchiectasis) — verified via OMIM (J47, UMLS C0006267)
- SNOMED 233604007 (Pneumonia) — used in Synthea base modules
- SNOMED 91302008 (Sepsis) — used in Synthea base modules
- LOINC 2465-3 (IgG), 2458-8 (IgA), 2472-9 (IgM) — verified via loinc.org + ARUP + Labcorp
- RxNorm 1809414 (immunoglobulin G, human 10% in 50 mL Injection) — verified via NLM RxNorm-NDC crosswalk (Octagam, Privigen)
- NUBC discharge code 01 (Discharged to home) — standard NUBC value
Rate sources (added 2026-08):
- Incidence gate 0.0006: Boyle JM, Buckley RH. Population prevalence of diagnosed primary
immunodeficiency diseases in the United States. J Clin Immunol. 2007;27(5):497-502
(household survey, diagnosed PID prevalence ~1 in 1,200).
- Severity split (0.5/0.35/0.15 mild/moderate/severe): derived as a proxy from ESID Registry
(1994-2024, n=30,628; antibody deficiency 49%, combined immunodeficiency with syndromic
features 14%, CID alone 8%) and the 2020 Tandfonline systematic review of PID registries.
See the remark on Severity_Assignment for the derivation and its limits.
Seed all patients into PID risk assignment.
Onset of PID symptoms usually occurs in infancy or childhood, but some forms (e.g. CVID) are diagnosed in adulthood.
Severity 0-100 per GMF spec. Recurrent sinopulmonary, GI and skin infections are the cardinal feature of PID.
Common in combined immunodeficiencies and CVID; occurs in roughly half of patients.
More prominent in early-onset / severe forms (e.g. SCID, MHC class II deficiency).
Autoimmune cytopenias and enteropathy are recognised complications of CVID and other PIDs.
The condition is onset here but only diagnosed at the upcoming Primary_Care_Visit encounter.
Most patients are first seen in primary care or pediatrics.

discharge_disposition.display: Discharged to home care or self care (routine discharge)

remarks: Specialist immunology consultation.
Severity stratification is encoded as a distributed transition, not as data on the Observation itself.
Sourced as a severity proxy from PID-type registry composition, since no registry reports
mild/moderate/severe directly: ESID Registry (30,628 patients, 1994-2024) reports antibody
deficiencies -- generally the least severe category, though a minority (e.g. CVID) still need
IVIG -- at 49% of all diagnoses (55% in the European cohort, 78% in the US cohort); combined
immunodeficiency with syndromic features (14%) and CID alone (8%) are the categories that
usually require curative HSCT. Tandfonline 2020 systematic review of PID registries corroborates
antibody deficiency as the plurality/majority category worldwide. Mild=0.5 tracks the
antibody-deficiency-dominant literature share; Severe=0.15 sits below the ~15-22% combined
CID share since not all CID patients require transplant; Moderate=0.35 is the remainder
(symptomatic antibody deficiencies on IVIG, phagocyte defects, immune dysregulation).
This is a severity proxy derived from diagnostic-category shares, not a validated
clinical-severity study -- flagged here rather than left silently unsourced.

Serious infection requiring hospitalisation. Common organisms in PID include encapsulated bacteria (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae) and opportunistic pathogens.
SNOMED 50849002 is the canonical Synthea-wiki example for emergency-class encounters.

discharge_disposition.display: Discharged to home care or self care (routine discharge)

remarks: Chronic_Management loops back through Infection_Complication_Admission on each
recurrence (0.3/pass). Without ending the prior episode, HealthRecord.conditionStart's
de-dupe (present.containsKey(code)) means a second pneumonia episode on the same code
silently reuses the first episode's already-closed entry and is never attached to the
new admission's claim -- the second and later hospitalizations would carry no listed
diagnosis. Ending the condition at discharge lets each episode record its own entry.
Added so the bronchiectasis diagnosis below lands on its own encounter/claim instead of
silently reusing whatever encounter last happened to be open. HealthRecord.currentEncounter()
falls back to the most recent *past* encounter (even an already-closed one) when no encounter
is active, so a bare ConditionOnset here would attach a new-onset diagnosis to a stale,
already-discharged encounter from a prior visit.
Bronchiectasis is the prototypical chronic organ-damage complication of antibody-deficiency PIDs (especially CVID).
Verified via OMIM (ICD-10 J47, UMLS C0006267).
Modelled as a long-term sequela arising in the Chronic_Management branch.

Replaces the prior version's incorrect ConditionEnd state.
Symptomatic primary immunodeficiency affects roughly 1 in 1,200-2,000 people. Without this gate the module onsets PID in every patient and its mortality branches then kill most of them before 65.

Source: Boyle JM, Buckley RH. Population prevalence of diagnosed primary immunodeficiency diseases in the United States. J Clin Immunol. 2007;27(5):497-502 -- a national random-digit-dial household survey that found diagnosed PID prevalence of ~1 in 1,200 (0.083%). 0.0006 (1 in 1,667) is deliberately conservative within that study's estimate, since this module's downstream mortality/HSCT branches are calibrated to the diagnosed (symptomatic, worked-up) population the survey captured, not the larger undiagnosed-mild-deficiency population some other sources include.
